newsitem.title: USA: U.S. CRUDES TURN STRONGER, OUTRIGHTS FIRM IN GULF.
newsitem.headline: U.S. CRUDES TURN STRONGER, OUTRIGHTS FIRM IN GULF.

text.p: Crude prices in the U.S. Gulf advanced Tuesday ahead of the release of American Petroleum Institute (API) inventory data,
Cash grades gained as well, moving to firmer levels in both the sweet and sour sectors, mainly on refiner short covering and some strength in competitive North Sea crudes.
September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing talked late at $19.85-95 a barrel, some 20 cents stronger than Monday, but around 10 cents weaker than the NYMEX settlement.
API data put crude runs at 95 percent of capacity from 97.1 percent a week before, with crude stocks 2.75 million barrels higher and gasoline levels down 863,000 barrels.
Traders had expected a larger gasoline draw, pushing ACCESS aftermarket prices lower.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James held to a 16-20 cents premium to the September WTI, trading within that band most of the session.

Other prices had West Texas Sour/Midland at $1.44-40 under WTI, some six cents firmer than Monday. Even though Iraqi crude exports were all but started, there was some active refiner short covering behind the slight price rise.
"I guess when the oil from Iraq starts to hit the actual markets, then WTS will decline more," said a cash dealer.
Other trades had Postings Plus around the $1.90 mark, working off a September/October spread of minus 20-18 cents.

U.N. overseers have approved a total of six Iraqi crude contracts through Tuesday afternoon for a total of 35.02 million barrels. Overseers still have to process a dozen contracts that were faxed to their offices since Monday.
